source: Aquinas, Summa Theologica I.2.3 (First Way, condensed)
text: Some things in the world are in motion. Whatever is in motion is put in motion by something else, since nothing can move itself from potentiality to actuality except by something already actual. This chain of movers cannot regress infinitely, because without a first mover there would be no subsequent motion at all. Therefore there must exist a first, unmoved mover, which everyone understands to be God.

source: Aquinas, Summa Theologica I.2.3 (Second Way, condensed)
text: In the world we observe an order of efficient causes. Nothing can be the efficient cause of itself, for that would mean it existed before itself, which is impossible. Causes cannot regress infinitely, since removing the first cause removes all the intermediate and final causes. Therefore there must be a first efficient cause, which we call God.

source: Aquinas, Summa Theologica I.2.3 (Fifth Way / teleological, condensed)
text: We observe that natural bodies lacking intelligence, such as plants and animals, nevertheless act toward an end in a regular way, always or nearly always achieving the best result. Things without intelligence cannot tend toward an end unless directed by something with knowledge and intelligence, as an arrow is directed by an archer. Therefore some intelligent being exists that directs all natural things to their end, and this we call God.

Either God exists or God does not exist, and reason alone cannot settle the matter. If you wager that God exists and you are right, you gain infinite happiness; if you are wrong, you lose little. If you wager that God does not exist and you are wrong, you risk infinite loss; if you are right, you gain little. Given the possibility of infinite gain against finite loss, it is rational to wager that God exists.
Everything that begins to exist has a cause of its existence. The universe began to exist. Therefore, the universe has a cause of its existence.

God is defined as that being than which nothing greater can be conceived. It is greater to exist in reality than to exist only in the understanding. If God existed only in the understanding, then a greater being could be conceived, one that also exists in reality, which is a contradiction. Therefore God must exist in reality and not merely in the understanding.

If God is willing to prevent evil but not able, then God is not omnipotent. If God is able to prevent evil but not willing, then God is malevolent. If God is both able and willing, then why does evil exist? If God is neither able nor willing, then God is not worthy of the name. Therefore, either God is not omnipotent, not benevolent, or God does not exist as traditionally conceived.

Consider whether the pious is loved by the gods because it is pious, or whether it is pious because it is loved by the gods. If the gods love it because it is already pious, then piety must be something independent of their approval, and their love merely tracks an external standard. If instead it is pious only because the gods love it, then piety has no fixed nature of its own and could change if the gods' preferences changed. Either way, defining piety simply as 'what the gods love' fails to explain what piety actually is.

I can doubt the existence of my body, the external world, and even mathematical truths, since a deceiving demon might be misleading me about all of these. But I cannot doubt that I am thinking, because the very act of doubting is itself a form of thinking. And if I am thinking, something must exist that does the thinking. Therefore, I exist, at least as a thinking thing.

All our reasoning about matters of fact depends on the relation of cause and effect. Our belief that causes will continue to produce their usual effects rests only on the assumption that the future will resemble the past. But any argument for that assumption would itself have to appeal to past experience, which is the very thing in question. Therefore, our confidence that the future will resemble the past cannot be rationally justified by argument; it rests on habit rather than reason.

Jesus claimed to be the Son of God and to forgive sins. A man who made such claims, if they were false, would either know they were false, making him a liar, or would not know, making him a lunatic on the level of a man who believes he is a poached egg. A mere moral teacher would not make such claims. Since Jesus does not fit the profile of a liar or a lunatic, we are left concluding he was telling the truth: Lord, liar, or lunatic, and he must be Lord.

source: Genesis 1 creation narrative, teleological reading (condensed apologetic form)
text: The universe exhibits complex order and fine-tuned physical constants that permit life. Complex, fine-tuned order of this kind is, in every other case we know of, the product of intelligent design rather than chance. Therefore, it is reasonable to infer that the universe's order is the product of an intelligent designer.

Millions of people across history and cultures report direct experiences of the divine. In the absence of strong evidence that such experiences are unreliable, we should trust experiential reports in the same way we trust perceptual reports of the physical world. We have no strong general evidence that religious experience is unreliable. Therefore, we should give some evidential weight to religious experience as pointing toward the existence of God.

Human beings across cultures appeal to a common moral law that they feel bound to but did not invent. A law of this kind requires a lawgiver beyond human society to explain its authority and universality. If there were no such lawgiver, moral obligation would just be a matter of preference or social convention, yet moral obligation does not feel or function that way. Therefore, the existence of an objective moral law points to the existence of God.

source: Argument from prophecy fulfillment (condensed apologetic form)
text: The Hebrew scriptures contain specific predictions about a coming Messiah, including details about his birthplace, manner of death, and role. The New Testament accounts describe Jesus of Nazareth as fulfilling these specific predictions. The odds of a single individual fulfilling so many independent predictions by chance are extremely low. Therefore, the fulfillment of these prophecies provides evidence that Jesus was the foretold Messiah.

The Declaration of Independence states that all men are created equal. Slavery denies to an entire class of human beings the basic rights that declaration guarantees. A nation cannot claim to be founded on the principle of human equality while permitting the wholesale denial of that principle to millions of its people. Therefore, slavery is fundamentally incompatible with the founding principles of the nation and cannot be treated as a matter of indifference.

Factions arise whenever people have differing opinions, passions, or interests, and this is an unavoidable feature of free societies. There are only two ways to remove the causes of faction: removing liberty, which is worse than the disease, or giving every citizen identical opinions and interests, which is impossible. Since the causes of faction cannot be removed, the only remedy is to control its effects through a well-constructed republic that dilutes factional influence over a large, diverse population.

source: Martin Luther King Jr., Letter from Birmingham Jail (condensed)
text: An unjust law is a code that a numerical or power majority imposes on a minority that had no part in enacting or creating that law, since that minority was denied the right to vote. Alabama's laws that prevented Black citizens from registering to vote and participating in the political process were of this kind. Laws enacted through such an undemocratic process are unjust. Therefore, the segregation statutes enacted under these conditions are unjust laws, and it is not merely permissible but morally required to resist them.

Government is necessary because men are not angels and would not otherwise treat one another justly. But government itself must be controlled, because those who govern are not angels either. The most reliable way to control government is to construct it so that its own internal structure, through separated and competing powers, checks its own tendency toward abuse. Therefore, a constitution should be built on ambition counteracting ambition rather than relying on the good character of those in office.

In a sample of 500 ravens observed across twelve countries, every single one was black. No study has ever documented a naturally-colored non-black raven. Based on this consistent pattern, it is reasonable to conclude that all ravens are black.

Every restaurant this reviewer has visited in the small coastal town received consistently high marks for fresh seafood, five restaurants in total, all rated four stars or higher. It is reasonable to conclude that seafood quality is generally strong throughout the town's restaurants.

A new experimental drug produced strong pain relief with minimal side effects in laboratory mice, whose pain-signaling pathways closely resemble those of humans. Because mice and humans share this relevant physiological similarity, it is reasonable to expect the drug will produce similar pain relief with minimal side effects in human trials.

Cities that raised their minimum wage significantly over the past decade saw, on average, no measurable increase in unemployment relative to comparable cities that did not raise wages. This pattern has now been observed in multiple independent studies across different regions. It is reasonable to conclude that moderate minimum wage increases do not, by themselves, cause significant job losses.

The patient presents with a high fever, a stiff neck, and sensitivity to light. These three symptoms together are a well-established sign pattern strongly associated with bacterial meningitis. Therefore, it is reasonable for the physician to suspect meningitis and order a confirming test.

The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, composed of thousands of climate scientists who have reviewed decades of peer-reviewed research, concludes that human activity is the dominant cause of observed warming since the mid-20th century. Given the depth of expertise and evidence review behind this conclusion, it is reasonable for a non-expert to accept it as very likely true.
If it rained last night, the sidewalk would be wet. The sidewalk is wet. Therefore, it must have rained last night.
If a person studies hard, they will pass the exam. This student did not study hard. Therefore, this student will not pass the exam.

The senator's proposed budget plan cannot be trusted, because the senator was caught in a minor financial scandal years ago. A person with that kind of history has no credibility on financial matters. Therefore, the budget plan should be rejected.
I met two tourists from that country and both were rude to service staff. Clearly, people from that country tend to be rude to service staff.
Either we cut the education budget or the city will go bankrupt within a year. We cannot let the city go bankrupt. Therefore, we must cut the education budget.

Remote work has been shown across multiple large-scale studies to reduce commute-related emissions without harming measured productivity in knowledge-work roles. Given that climate goals require reducing transportation emissions and that employers have not shown a productivity cost, companies that still mandate full-time office attendance are choosing tradition over both evidence and stated environmental commitments.

source: original illustrative example, op-ed style, suppressed premise
text: The city council just approved another luxury condo development downtown. Given how many families here are already struggling to find affordable housing, this decision shows the council simply does not care about ordinary residents.
All men are mortal. Socrates is a man. Therefore, Socrates is mortal.

If the bridge is structurally unsound, it will be closed to traffic. If it is closed to traffic, commuters will need an alternate route. Therefore, if the bridge is structurally unsound, commuters will need an alternate route.
